title: Hulls of classical deformation functors
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use the test category $\mathrm{Art}_k=\mathcal C_{k,k}$, the groupoid pseudofunctors $\mathcal D$, their isomorphism classes $F(A)$, the tangent set $T=F(k[k])$, and complete Noetherian marked local $k$-algebras $B$ of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Write $k[V]=k\oplus V$ with square-zero second summand, and $F(f)$ for transport on isomorphism classes [def-sfb-artin-square-zero-transport]. A vector-space structure on $T$ has the classical tangent operations when $ax=F(k[a\mathrm{id}_k])(x)$ and, for every $z\in F(k[k\times k])$, $F(k[\mathrm{fst}+\mathrm{snd}])(z)=F(k[\mathrm{fst}])(z)+F(k[\mathrm{snd}])(z)$. Put $h_B(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{res}}(B,A)$; these maps are continuous for the maximal-ideal-adic topologies because the target maximal ideal is nilpotent. A natural class map $\eta:h_B\to F$ consists of maps $\eta_A:h_B(A)\to F(A)$ commuting with every marked test morphism. The canonical vector operations on $T h_B=h_B(k[k])$ are characterized by the pointwise addition and scalar multiplication of the epsilon coefficients of the local maps. A class map is a hull if, for every surjection $f:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, every $a\in h_B(A)$ and $y\in F(A')$ with $\eta_A(a)=F(f)(y)$ have a lift $b\in h_B(A')$ with $fb=a$ and $\eta_{A'}(b)=y$, and its tangent component is a $k$-linear isomorphism for these canonical operations. A class map is a natural isomorphism when its components have inverse maps, with both inverse identities and naturality of the inverses. The canonical zero-section arrow $k\to k[k]$ sends $a$ to $(a,0)$; transporting $x_0\in\mathcal D(k)$ along it gives the trivial first-order deformation whose automorphism group is $\operatorname{Inf}(\mathcal D)$.
